cues.zh: 上世纪30年代初，有个叫伯尔赫斯·弗雷德里克·斯金纳的人
cues.en: In the early 1930s a man named Burrhus Frederic Skinner

cues.zh: 开始以一种全新的激进方式研究心理学。
cues.en: began to study psychology in a radical new way.

cues.zh: 在他之前，我们只知道如何建立条件反射；
cues.en: See, before him we only knew how to condition reactions;

cues.zh: 我们可以让人条件反射地害怕南瓜，或者一看到办公用品就饿。
cues.en: we could condition a person to be terrified of pumpkins or hungry at the sight of office supplies.

cues.zh: 但斯金纳推断，你还能更进一步。
cues.en: But Skinner theorized that you could go one further.

cues.zh: 他推断，你可以对意志本身进行条件反射——你可以改变人们做选择的方式
cues.en: He theorized that you could condition volition—that you could change the way that people make choices

cues.zh: 那我们为什么要聊这个？因为如今大量的游戏
cues.en: So why are we talking about it? Because a vast number of today's games are

cues.zh: 都建立在斯金纳的发现之上，而这正在变成一种坏习惯。
cues.en: built upon Skinner's discoveries, and it's starting to become a bad habit.

cues.zh: 不过，在我扯得太远之前，我们先仔细看看斯金纳到底做了什么。
cues.en: But, before I get ahead of myself, let's take a closer look at what Skinner did.

cues.zh: 斯金纳造了一台机器：一个简单的箱子，里面有个按钮，他会把鸽子放进去。
cues.en: Skinner created a machine: a simple box with a button in it that he would put pigeons in.

cues.zh: 当鸽子啄按钮时，机器就会给它们食物。
cues.en: When the pigeons pecked at the button the machine would give them food.

cues.zh: 然后他把盒子连接到一台记录设备上，这样就能知道鸽子多久啄一次按钮。
cues.en: He then hooked the box up to a recording device so he could tell how often the pigeons pecked the button.

cues.zh: 听起来挺简单，那么：为什么这如此具有突破性？
cues.en: Seems simple enough, so: why was this so groundbreaking?

cues.zh: 因为啄按钮是主动行为。
cues.en: Because pecking the button is active.

cues.zh: 这不只是对刺激的自动反应，它涉及做出决定。
cues.en: This wasn't just an automatic reaction to stimuli, it involved making a decision.

cues.zh: 所以如果斯金纳能证明他可以稳定地改变鸽子啄按钮的频率，
cues.en: So if Skinner could show that he could consistently change how often the pigeons peck the button,

cues.zh: 他就能证明他可以训练它们做出特定的选择。
cues.en: he could show that he could condition them to make a specific choice.

cues.zh: 这被称为操作性条件反射。
cues.en: This is called operant conditioning.

cues.zh: 他的发现有两个惊人的部分。
cues.en: Now there were two amazing parts to his findings.

cues.zh: 第一，操作性条件反射对人类也有效。
cues.en: One, operant conditioning works on humans.

cues.zh: 第二，每次做某个动作就给予奖励，
cues.en: Two, simply rewarding someone every time they do an action

cues.zh: 并不是让他们持续做那个动作的最佳方式。
cues.en: isn't the best way to keep them continually doing that action.

cues.zh: 相反，如果一个人随机重复多次某个动作后，你才给他奖励，
cues.en: Rather, if you provide a reward to a person after they perform the action a random number of times,

cues.zh: 或者每隔若干分钟才给一次奖励，
cues.en: or only give a reward once every so many minutes,

cues.zh: 这些方法更能让人养成重复某个动作的习惯。
cues.en: these methods are far more effective at conditioning someone to repeat an action.

cues.zh: 斯金纳常用赌博来讲解操作性条件作用。
cues.en: Skinner often talked about operant conditioning in terms of gambling.

cues.zh: 大多数赌博游戏都不会让赌徒占便宜，奇怪的是，大多数赌徒也很清楚这一点，
cues.en: Most gambling games are not rigged in the gambler's favor and, oddly enough, most gamblers are well aware of this,

cues.zh: 可他们还是继续赌博，而不去做一份
cues.en: and yet they continue to gamble rather than perform an

cues.zh: 同样费力、收入固定、净收入却更高的工作。
cues.en: equally strenuous job that has a regular pay out with a higher net profit.

cues.zh: 想想看，人们会觉得哪种活动更有趣：
cues.en: Consider which activity people will tell you is more fun:

cues.zh: 在赌场玩老虎机八个小时，最后赢一百美元，
cues.en: spending eight hours in a casino playing the slots and ending up with a hundred bucks,

cues.zh: 还是在工厂按八个小时按钮，最后领到一张一百美元的工资？
cues.en: or pushing a button in a factory for eight hours and getting a paycheck for a hundred bucks at the end.

cues.zh: 这一切还被斯金纳研究中的另一个发现进一步放大了：
cues.en: This is all compounded by another discovery of Skinner's research:

cues.zh: 他证明了初级强化物，即满足基本生理需求的奖励——
cues.en: he demonstrated that primary conditioners, or rewards that are fundamental biological needs—

cues.zh: 你知道的：食物、水、性等等——一旦人达到“饱足”，
cues.en: you know: food water sex etc.—have a diminishing effect once a person reaches "satiation,"

cues.zh: 也就是其生理需求的极限，效果就会递减。
cues.en: or the biological limit of their needs.

cues.zh: 但还有次级强化物：生理领域之外的东西，
cues.en: But then there are secondary reinforcers: things outside the biological realm,

cues.zh: 比如金钱或社会认可。这些东西通常不会触及饱足点。
cues.en: like money or social approbation. These things generally don't hit a satiation point.

cues.zh: 你大概能看出这要引向哪里了。
cues.en: You can probably see where we're going with this.

cues.zh: 你们很多人都玩过《农场小镇》或《魔兽世界》，玩到早就没了乐趣还继续玩。
cues.en: Many of you have played Farmville or World of Warcraft well past the point where it was fun.

cues.zh: 为什么？
cues.en: Why?

cues.zh: 因为这些游戏非常明显是围绕奖励时间表设计的。
cues.en: Because those games are very clearly built around reward schedules.

cues.zh: 这两款游戏的整个设计，就是要让你形成条件反射，持续重复
cues.en: The entire design of both of those games is to condition you to continue to repeat

cues.zh: 一个早已失去新鲜感的动作——
cues.en: an action that has long since lost its novelty—

cues.zh: 一个早已变得枯燥乏味的动作。
cues.en: that has long since become tedious.

cues.zh: 其实，在继续之前：先快速声明一下。
cues.en: Actually, before we continue: quick disclaimer.

cues.zh: 被训练成条件反射地做某件事，和真正上瘾，是完全不同的。
cues.en: Being conditioned to do an action and being addicted to something are very different.

cues.zh: 今天我们不深入讲上瘾的问题，我只是想先点明这个区别。
cues.en: We're not gonna go into the addiction thing today but I just wanted to acknowledge the difference.

cues.zh: 今天我们要讲的，只是游戏如何对我们进行条件反射训练。
cues.en: All we're going to talk about today is how games can condition us.

cues.zh: 好了，声明结束。
cues.en: Okay, disclaimer over.

cues.zh: 那么，如果游戏这么做，问题出在哪？
cues.en: So why is it a problem if games do this?

cues.zh: 先暂且不谈用斯金纳理论做游戏在道德上的争议。
cues.en: For now let's ignore the questionable morality of using Skinner's theories to create games.

cues.zh: 问题在于，这是一种懒惰又廉价的方式，让人误以为自己享受你的产品。
cues.en: The problem is that it's a lazy and cheap way to get someone to believe they're enjoying your product.

cues.zh: 你有没有过这种经历：通关一款游戏，几周后回头一想，然后想，
cues.en: Have you ever finished a game and then looked back a few weeks later and thought,

cues.zh: “我到底在干什么，把人生80个小时砸进那玩意里？”
cues.en: "What the hell was I doing putting 80 hours of my life into that?

cues.zh: 这通常是因为游戏用了斯金纳的手法，
cues.en: That usually happens because the game used Skinner's techniques

cues.zh: 制造出投入的错觉，并拉长游玩时间。
cues.en: to create the illusion of engagement and extend playtime.

cues.zh: RPG游戏，尤其是做得差的那些，就是很好的例子。
cues.en: RPGs, especially poorly-made ones, are a great example of this.

cues.zh: 从掉落物品到升级，都是非常清晰的奖励机制，
cues.en: Everything from loot drops to leveling is a very clear reward schedule that

cues.zh: 强化了让你获得奖励的行为。
cues.en: reinforces the behavior that gets you the reward.

cues.zh: 有没有试过玩到很晚已经困了，但还是决定再升一级就睡
cues.en: ever been playing late and getting sleepy but then decide that you're going to get just one more level before you go to bed

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: Yep.

cues.zh: 但这不只是RPG游戏的问题，它普遍存在。
cues.en: But this isn't just an RPG problem, it's endemic.

cues.zh: 几乎所有带积分的游戏都用这套系统。
cues.en: Almost anything with points uses this system.

cues.zh: 改天问问你奶奶为什么那么爱玩《宝石迷阵》。
cues.en: Ask your grandmother sometime why she plays so much Bejeweled.

cues.zh: 但这也不仅限于积分。任何有清晰明确奖励的东西都适用。
cues.en: But it goes beyond points, too. It works with anything that has a clear and manifest reward.

cues.zh: 《纸牌接龙》——世界上玩得最多的游戏——把偶尔获胜设定为清晰的奖励
cues.en: Solitaire the most played game in the world sets up the infrequent win as a clear reward

cues.zh: 许多动作游戏用同样的系统让玩家连续12小时狂按同样的按钮。
cues.en: Many action games use the same system to convince players to mash the same buttons for 12 hours straight.

cues.zh: 就连射击游戏里那些告诉玩家有多厉害的语音旁白，也能被用作条件反射的工具。
cues.en: Even elements like the voiceovers in shooters that tell the player how awesome they are can be used as conditioning tools.

cues.zh: 这也是如今每款游戏都在加入RPG元素的主要原因之一。
cues.en: It's also one of the main reasons every game is getting RPG elements these days.

cues.zh: 别误会，加入RPG元素本身没问题，只要
cues.en: Now don't get me wrong, there's nothing wrong with adding RPG elements if it's

cues.zh: 是用来为游戏打造深度沉浸的系统。
cues.en: being used to create deep immersive systems for the game.

cues.zh: 其实我很喜欢这股趋势，当它是用来结合
cues.en: I'm actually a huge fan of this trend when it's used to combine

cues.zh: 心智挑战和操作挑战的时候，比如《使命召唤》或《地下城与勇士》。
cues.en: mental challenges and execution challenges like in Call of Duty or Dungeon Fighter.

cues.zh: 但太多游戏把RPG元素当成了拐杖。
cues.en: But too many games are using RPG elements as a crutch.

cues.zh: 平庸乏味的游戏会加入奖励系统，只是为了拖延你发现它有多糟糕。
cues.en: Bland uninspired games will include reward systems simply to delay your realization of how terrible they are.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，还有别的更好的方式能培养参与感，
cues.en: My point is there are other better ways of fostering engagement,

cues.zh: 而这些才是我们应该向游戏要求的，而不是简单的斯金纳箱式满足。
cues.en: and those are the methods we should be demanding from our games, not simple Skinner box satisfaction.

cues.zh: 以下是几个例子。
cues.en: Here are a few examples.

cues.zh: 1. 神秘感。
cues.en: 1. Mystery.

cues.zh: 人类的好奇心是一种强大的力量。
cues.en: Human curiosity is a powerful thing.

cues.zh: 我们喜欢解开谜团。
cues.en: We like unraveling mysteries.

cues.zh: 我们都玩过那种让我们忍不住问“这到底是怎么回事？”的游戏。
cues.en: We've all played a game that made us ask "what the hell's going on?"

cues.zh: 紧接着就想“我要继续玩下去，弄个明白。”
cues.en: immediately followed by "I want to keep going to find out."

cues.zh: 2. 精通。
cues.en: 2. Mastery.

cues.zh: 让玩家投入的方法，是给他机会精通一项技能，
cues.en: The player can be engaged by giving him the opportunity to master a skill,

cues.zh: 然后运用这份精通。
cues.en: and then utilize that mastery.

cues.zh: 你在音游、格斗游戏，有时甚至RPG里都能看到这种设计。
cues.en: You see this sort of thing in rhythm games fighting games sometimes even RPGs.

cues.zh: 这个在传统游戏里做起来有点难，但
cues.en: This one's a little tougher to execute in traditional games but

cues.zh: 我们在轻松游戏那期已经聊过了，所以：下一个！
cues.en: we already kind of talked about this in our easy games episode, so: moving on!

cues.zh: 3. 心智挑战。
cues.en: 3. Mental Challenge.

cues.zh: 说来奇怪，我们大多数人一天里其实并没有得到足够的心智刺激。
cues.en: Oddly enough most of us don't actually get enough mental stimulation in a day.

cues.zh: 从《雷顿教授》或《神秘岛》里的思考谜题，到《文明》游戏里碾压式的逻辑推演。
cues.en: From the thought problems in Professor Layton or Myst to the logic stomping of a Civ game.

cues.zh: 让玩家动脑思考，是保持他们兴趣的好办法。
cues.en: Giving players a way to work their brains is a great way to keep people interested.

cues.zh: 4. 叙事。
cues.en: 4. Narrative.

cues.zh: 你有没有曾经迷失在一个世界里？仅仅因为那是你想待的地方，就一直玩下去？
cues.en: You ever get lost in a world? Continued playing a game just because it was a place you wanted to be?

cues.zh: 这一点，以及线性故事叙事，都是吸引玩家的好方法。
cues.en: This, as well as linear story narrative, is a great way to engage players.

cues.zh: 5. 新奇感。
cues.en: 5. Novelty.

cues.zh: 这一点很难维持，但：人类喜欢新事物。我们会被新奇感吸引。
cues.en: This one's hard to maintain but: human beings like new things. We're engaged by novelty.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么棕色射击游戏会让人腻味，而《异域镇魂曲》不会。
cues.en: This is why brown shooters may wear thin but Planescape doesn't.

cues.zh: 6. 心流。
cues.en: 6. Flow.

cues.zh: 像《Everyday Shooter》、N₂O，甚至一场非常棒的
cues.en: Games like "everyday shooter," N₂O or even a really good session of

cues.zh: 初代《异形大战铁血战士》游戏，都能把玩家带入一种禅定状态。
cues.en: the original Alien vs Predator can bring a player to a sort of Zen trance.

cues.zh: 我们或多或少都经历过。
cues.en: We've all been there at one point or another.

cues.zh: 你的眼睛进入柔焦状态，眨眼变慢，
cues.en: Your eyes enter soft focus, your blinking slows,

cues.zh: 呼吸变得极其规律，你只是在做。
cues.en: your breathing becomes incredibly regular, and you're just doing.

cues.zh: 没有控制器；你和屏幕融为一体。
cues.en: There is no controller; you and the screen are one.

cues.zh: 你不再以普通的认知方式思考，而是在更深层次上运作。
cues.en: You've stopped thinking in the ordinary sense of cognition and instead are working on some much deeper level.

cues.zh: 这非常难以设计。
cues.en: This is very hard to design for.

cues.zh: 它本质上是在游玩中创造节奏，
cues.en: It basically involves creating rhythm within play,

cues.zh: 然后慢慢要求玩家开始更快地执行动作，
cues.en: and then slowly demanding the player to start performing actions faster,

cues.zh: 越来越快，积累势头，直到他们执行动作的速度
cues.en: and faster, building momentum until they're performing the actions

cues.zh: 快过他们可能思考的速度。
cues.en: faster than they could possibly think through them.

cues.zh: 作为设计师很难做到这一点，但在游戏中实现这种体验非常有吸引力。
cues.en: It's hard to pull this off as a designer but achieving this experience is deeply compelling in a game.

cues.zh: 这只是让游戏变得有趣的少数非条件化方法之一，
cues.en: Now this is just a small set of non-conditioning ways to make games fun,

cues.zh: 没有好游戏严格依赖其中一种；你最爱的游戏大多结合了许多这些元素。
cues.en: and no good game relies strictly on one; most of your favorites combine many of these elements.

cues.zh: 所以，致所有设计师和未来的设计师：
cues.en: So to all designers and future designers out there:

cues.zh: 我们必须摆脱这种日益依赖斯金纳箱式方法、迫使玩家玩我们游戏的做法。
cues.en: we have to get away from this increased reliance on Skinner box methods of compelling gamers to play our games.

cues.zh: 参与感和强迫性是两回事。
cues.en: Engagement and compulsion are different things.

cues.zh: 能做出让人着迷的体验，并不代表它就是好游戏。
cues.en: Just because you can make an experience compelling doesn't make it a good game.

cues.zh: 好了，感谢收看！下周见。
cues.en: Well, thanks for watching! See you next week.
